title: Contextual StereoSet: Stress-Testing Bias Alignment Robustness in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Multiple-choice stereotype association tests using the Contextual StereoSet benchmark, measuring stereotype selection rates across varying contextual framings such as location, year, communication style, and observer similarity.

Counterfactual name and background substitution (e.g., using names signaling specific racial groups or historical diversity context) in high-stakes vignettes involving hiring and police help-seeking to observe shifts in model recommendations.

Comparing model loan approval recommendations across small business lending vignettes with varying applicant names and explicit religious community affiliations (e.g., Hindu temple, Lutheran church, local mosque).
Evaluating model preferences in hiring vignettes by contrasting candidates with elite academic/legacy backgrounds against those with working-class, state school, or first-generation college profiles.
